candidates.basis: Ledger.grant and Ledger.revoke, both introduced by this change (absent at merge-base 2301c83, where ledger/accounts.py has no grant/revoke/delegate code at all), each inline an identical ownership comparison (`if account.owner != user: raise LedgerError(...)`) rather than calling into ledger/auth.py, which AGENTS.md:7 designates as the sole home for authorization decisions and which already encapsulates the equivalent owner-equality check inside can_view's fallback branch (`return account.owner == user`). The check is duplicated verbatim across the two new methods, so a future change to who may administer delegates requires editing accounts.py in two places instead of auth.py once.

candidates.basis: Ledger.grant and Ledger.revoke each call self.get(number) before the ownership check (accounts.py:54 and :61), and Ledger.get's own docstring states it 'Raises LedgerError when it does not exist' (accounts.py:46), so an unknown account number raises before the owner comparison is ever reached. Yet grant's and revoke's docstrings state only 'Raises LedgerError unless user owns the account,' omitting the unknown-account case, while sibling methods post and transfer (which also call self.get/get twice) enumerate 'an unknown account' explicitly in their docstrings, matching the explicit repository convention at AGENTS.md:6 that every public function's docstring names the errors it raises. This is new text written for these new methods, not a pre-existing omission.
